newsitem.title: GERMANY: Seles fails again to get tougher term for attacker.
newsitem.headline: Seles fails again to get tougher term for attacker.

text.p: Tennis star Monica Seles has failed in a final bid to get a stiffer sentence for the attacker who stabbed her at a German tournament in 1993 and kept her out of the sport for more than two years.

A spokeswoman for justice authorities in Hamburg said on Wednesday the city's highest court had upheld the judgment of two previous courts which gave lathe operator Guenter Parche a two-year suspended sentence for causing grievous bodily harm.
Lawyers for Seles had wanted Parche convicted for attemped manslaughter and given a much tougher sentence.
Parche, an obsessive fan of Seles's German rival Steffi Graf, leapt from the stands during a break in play at the April 1993 Hamburg Open and plunged a kitchen knife into her back.
The judge at Parche's original trial in October 1993 ruled that he was emotionally retarded and might not have been entirely responsible for his actions.
Parche said his fascination with Graf drove him to attack Seles -- then ranked number one in the world -- to help Graf regain the top spot.
Seles said in a written submission to the original appeal hearing in 1995 that the attack had ruined her life.

Suffering from fear and depression, she several times postponed her comeback to the international tennis circuit and finally returned in 1995. She has not taken part in any tournaments in Germany since her comeback.
The latest decision followed another rebuff for Seles last December by a German court, which rejected her claim for damages from the organisers of the Hamburg tournament.
